academicReview: Arts,culturalobjects,interpretation and historical/social/theoretical contexts define the degree. Allthree routes contain sustained direct arts/literature/media study. Threeinstitutionalpolitics courses are replaced to protect that substance; generalcoherence alone is insufficient. Music/theatre/festival and independentthesis gaps remain visible.

courseReview.name: Personal & Professional Development
courseReview.contribution: Mandatory first-year development.

courseReview.name: Modern History
courseReview.contribution: provides historical analysis of political, social and cultural transformation

courseReview.name: Histories of Gender
courseReview.contribution: Direct cultural and historical analysis: gendered American lives, storytelling, queer activism and cultural expressions are studied from the nineteenth century onward.

courseReview.name: History of Empires
courseReview.contribution: examines empires, power, oppression and competing historical interpretations

courseReview.name: History Research Seminar
courseReview.contribution: Complementary research method: students analyse diaries, letters, memoirs and official reports concerning the 1809 Walcheren Expedition and write a substantial paper. The military-history topic is fixed; this is not a freely chosen arts-and-culture thesis.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courseReview.contribution: Complementary philosophical method: central questions about knowledge, reality, responsibility and freedom develop critical reasoning and argument. The enriched syllabus does not establish a dedicated aesthetics component.

courseReview.name: Ethics
courseReview.contribution: Complementary ethical reasoning: moral theories, responsibility, equality and historical injustice support critical judgments about cultural institutions and representation; ethics is not a substitute for aesthetics.

courseReview.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courseReview.contribution: examines emotion, experience and agency as dimensions of cultural meaning

courseReview.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
courseReview.contribution: examines political authority, freedom, equality and competing justifications of power

courseReview.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
courseReview.contribution: Generic institutional or international politics gives inadequate cultural-object analysis for this target; replaced with direct art, stylistics and adaptation.

courseReview.name: Theory of International Relations
courseReview.contribution: Generic institutional or international politics gives inadequate cultural-object analysis for this target; replaced with direct art, stylistics and adaptation.

courseReview.name: European Union Politics
courseReview.contribution: Generic institutional or international politics gives inadequate cultural-object analysis for this target; replaced with direct art, stylistics and adaptation.

courseReview.name: Peace & Conflict
courseReview.contribution: Complementary political-cultural context: theories of conflict consider ideology, identity-based grievances, colonial histories and justice/reconciliation across institutional and cultural perspectives; it is not an arts-analysis course.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Sociology
courseReview.contribution: introduces analysis of institutions, identities, inequality and social interaction

courseReview.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courseReview.contribution: develops qualitative research design, interpretation and reflexive analysis for cultural inquiry

courseReview.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
courseReview.contribution: uses feminist, anti-colonial and justice perspectives to study social movements and public action

courseReview.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courseReview.contribution: Direct complementary theory of public culture: Gramsci, Habermas, Fraser, civil society, solidarity, the public sphere and decolonial critique support interpretation of cultural power. The empirical project studies a civil-society organisation, rather than a guaranteed arts institution.

courseReview.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courseReview.contribution: develops rhetorical analysis, argument, writing and presentation for cultural criticism

courseReview.name: Style & Meaning
courseReview.contribution: examines how style produces meaning and develops precise critical writing

courseReview.name: Communicating the Climate Crisis
courseReview.contribution: analyses texts, films, exhibitions, protest art and social media in contested public debate

courseReview.name: Persuasive Communication
courseReview.contribution: Complementary public communication: framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and persuasion ethics develop analysis and application of influence in science, society and sustainability. The local-institution project is not guaranteed to concern arts organisations.

courseReview.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
courseReview.contribution: Direct creative-cultural analysis and practice: poetry, rhythm, voice, embodiment and hybrid projects connect interpretation with making. Music performance, singing and songwriting are expressly excluded; no festival-production or performing-arts qualification is claimed.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Western Art History
courseReview.contribution: introduces visual and art-historical analysis across historical contexts

courseReview.name: Introduction to World Archaeology
courseReview.contribution: studies material culture and identity across societies from a world-archaeological perspective

courseReview.name: African Art & Heritage
courseReview.contribution: examines African art and heritage through historical, social and postcolonial contexts

courseReview.name: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean
courseReview.contribution: studies Renaissance art in connected Mediterranean and global historical contexts

courseReview.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
courseReview.contribution: examines modern art, museums and institutions that shape cultural value and meaning

courseReview.name: Heritage & Ancient Democracy
courseReview.contribution: connects art, literature, architecture and heritage with democracy, inclusion and political participation

courseReview.name: Writing Art's Histories
courseReview.contribution: Direct cultural theory and method: historiography from Vasari through Warburg, Panofsky, Gombrich, Foucault and Derrida examines aesthetics, authorship, identity and art-historical interpretation. No independent primary-research project is asserted.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
courseReview.contribution: introduces close reading, literary interpretation and critical analysis of cultural texts

courseReview.name: Great Literary Works
courseReview.contribution: Direct literary repertoire and interpretation: a chronological survey from Gilgamesh to postmodernity mainly addresses Western literary heritage and its cultural themes. Global breadth is supplied by World Myth & Literature and other courses, not attributed to this course alone.

courseReview.name: World Myth & Literature
courseReview.contribution: compares myth and literature across cultures, periods and media

courseReview.name: Life & Travel Writing
courseReview.contribution: analyses how life and travel writing construct identity, place and intercultural encounters

courseReview.name: Film & Text
courseReview.contribution: studies relations between film and text, including adaptation and medium-specific meaning

courseReview.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
courseReview.contribution: examines competing theories and practices of literary meaning and interpretation

courseReview.name: Introduction to Film & Media
courseReview.contribution: introduces film and media forms, histories and analytical concepts

courseReview.name: Media Archaeology
courseReview.contribution: examines media histories, technologies and changing material forms

courseReview.name: Media & the Environment
courseReview.contribution: analyses how visual and audiovisual media construct environmental meaning across cultural and postcolonial contexts

courseReview.name: Media & Race
courseReview.contribution: Direct media and cultural analysis: American racial histories, photographs, film and music examine systemic racism, representation, power and resistance; the final podcast is research-grounded.

courseReview.name: The Documentary
courseReview.contribution: examines documentary form, evidence, representation and creative non-fiction practice
